title: Perché apre la finestra ma non mi fa vedere il contenuto del messaggio?
creator: aerotecnicastar
content:
Un file salvato da thunderbird con estensione .eml non viene correttamente aperto da thunderbird. Si apre la finestra ma non si riesce a leggere il contenuto. L'unico modo per leggerlo è copiarlo in una cartella di thunderbird. In quel modo il messaggio viene letto. Con una versione precedentemente installata ciò non accadeva. E' possibile risolvere questa cosa e tornare a leggere i messaggi senza doverli per forza importare?

An email saved from Thunderbird as an .eml file can no longer be opened properly in Thunderbird. The message window opens, but the email content is not displayed, making it impossible to read.

The only workaround is to copy the .eml file into one of Thunderbird's mail folders. Once imported this way, the message can be opened and read normally.

This issue did not occur with the previously installed version of Thunderbird.

Is there a way to fix this and restore the ability to open and read .eml files directly, without having to import them into Thunderbird first?

title: All emails show up with this line "this is a draft message" under the subject line.
creator: mozilla638
content:
I have about a dozen accounts with over 50 folders, most with a matching filter. About 100k messages, taking up about 1G of disk space. All but one account is merged under my Inbox to have fewer duplicate In/Draft/Sent boxes eating up window space. I'm using 152.0.1 (aarch64) Release branch on a Mac OS X 26. All are POP accounts on a DreamHost server.

At some point it started to show the draft message on every email, which means on incoming as well. I've had this phenomenon for years.

Recently filtering has started to not automatically run on some emails forcing me to run the filters manually. I've run the repair folder options which does not seem to make any difference.

Since switching to macOS 26 it also does not allow me to move Thunderbird child windows, they simply show up on the default location. But that's for another ticket.
